cover_letter:
Dear Whale team,

I'm writing to apply for the SEO Specialist role. Whale's mission to become the go-to answer for "which SOP tool is best" resonates with me—I work where SEO, content, and web meet, and I'm fascinated by how AI-powered search is reshaping organic visibility.

In my current freelance work and as a Junior Digital Marketer at Episto, I handle on-page SEO, keyword research, and SEO content for client websites, tracking results with Ahrefs, Semrush, Google Analytics, and Search Console. I've built and optimized WordPress sites from the ground up, implementing JSON-LD schema, knowledge-graph markup, and llms.txt files, and running iterative technical SEO/GEO audits that measurably raised search-health scores. For mirook.com, I used structured data and entity optimization to improve visibility in both traditional and AI-driven search.

I use Ahrefs daily—Site Explorer, Content Explorer, and Link Intersect—to analyze competitors and identify link opportunities. I understand that AI models pull from listicles, editorial mentions, and Reddit threads, and I'm eager to earn Whale a place in those high-traffic sources. I've also built repeatable AI content systems, using LLMs for research, content creation, and audits, and automating repetitive tasks with Python and MCP integrations.

What draws me to Whale is the emphasis on link quality over raw traffic and the clear ownership of authority, content, citations, and on-page work. I stay organized with multiple projects in flight, from outreach pipelines to content calendars, and I thrive in fast-moving environments. I'm excited about the opportunity to help Whale unlock organic growth and turn up every time someone asks which SOP tool is best.

Thank you for considering my application. I'd welcome the chance to discuss how my skills can contribute to Whale's next stage of growth.

Sincerely,
Baver Ok
